advances: Local base-moment correction under positive interior loss means. Depth is a separate constraint.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Work in the $k$-dimensional span of the $d_z=z-j$, extending linear parameters to the original base space when needed. The positive original weights put $j$ in the relative interior. For $z\in P$ write $S_z=\mathcal H^{d-1}(\partial A_z)$ and $q_z=(1,d_z)$. For $d=1$, $S_z=2$. Define $F_t(h,v)$ to be $\sum_z q_z$ times the respective removed fiber volume divided by $\delta_t$, using radii $b_z=\delta_t e^{h+v\cdot d_z}$. By the convex erosion lemma these are the removals of an actual convex body.

For a convex body $K$ with positive inradius and $0\le b$ smaller than its inradius, the loss $|K|-|K[-b]|$ is $\int_0^b \mathcal H^{d-1}(\partial K[-w])\,dw$ by coarea for the distance to its boundary. The interior distance has gradient norm one almost everywhere where it is differentiable and positive, and its nonmaximal positive levels are boundaries of the eroded bodies. The bodies $K[-w]$ are continuous in $w$ below the inradius: if $K[-w]$ contains a ball of radius $R>0$, a homothet of ratio $1-\varepsilon/R$ about that ball's center is contained in $K[-(w+\varepsilon)]$, by convexity and the inner ball. This also gives the left limit. Convex surface area is Hausdorff continuous on full-dimensional convex bodies by the Cauchy projection formula, or is the constant two in dimension one. Thus the loss derivative in $b$ equals the surface area at radius $b$.

The finitely many input fibers contain fixed balls of uniformly positive radius from the old fibers. On any compact parameter set the $b_z$ tend uniformly to zero, and the inner homothets about the fixed ball centers show that all corresponding eroded fibers converge uniformly to $A_z$. Applying the surface-area derivative and the chain rule gives $C^1$ convergence on compact parameter sets to
$$
 F_0(h,v)=\sum_z S_z e^{h+v\cdot d_z}q_z.
$$
In particular the first derivatives follow from multiplying each current eroded surface area by $e^{h+v\cdot d_z}q_z q_z^\mathsf T$ in the Jacobian.

To solve $F_0=(\kappa,r-j)$, minimize $\log\sum_z S_z e^{v\cdot d_z}-v\cdot(r-j)/\kappa$. Its Hessian is the covariance of the $d_z$ under positive weights, positive definite on the span because the sites affinely span it. The interior condition gives a ball of some radius $\eta>0$ about the desired mean in $\operatorname{conv}\{d_z\}$, so the expression is at least $\eta\|v\|+\log\min_zS_z$. There is a unique minimizer; choose $h$ to set the total to $\kappa$. For $k=0$ omit the $v$ minimization. At the solution $(h_0,v_0)$ the Jacobian $J=\sum_z S_ze^{h_0+v_0\cdot d_z}q_zq_z^\mathsf T$ is positive definite since the $q_z$ span. On a small fixed closed ball about the solution, $x\mapsto x-J^{-1}[F_t(x)-(\kappa,r_t-j)]$ has Lipschitz constant less than one for small $t$ and maps the ball into itself because the displacement of its center tends to zero. Its fixed point solves the exact scaled moments and converges to $(h_0,v_0)$. For a compact set of target means, the same local neighborhoods for targets near each point and a finite subcover give uniform existence.

Set $s_t=\delta_t e^{h_t}$. The positive inballs persist, and the computed removal mass and moments give the asserted retained mass and base centroid. Any $r-j$ whose gauge in $\operatorname{conv}(P)-j$ is less than $\kappa$ meets the interior condition, including rank zero. Conversely if additions concentrate on a proper exposed face of $\operatorname{conv}P$, an exposing linear functional centered at $j$ has a positive maximum there; matching the added moment in that direction using removals on $P$ requires removal mass at least the added mass.
statement: Let a compact convex source $D$ have positive $d$-dimensional integer fibers $A_z$ on a finite lattice-convex set $P$ and integer true mixed centroid base $j$. Write $m=\sum_{z\in P}|A_z|$. Suppose compact convex enlargements $E_t\supseteq D$ have the same positive integer bases, $(E_t)_z\to A_z$ in Hausdorff distance for all $z\in P$, and added mixed mass $\delta_t\to0$ through positive values, with added base means $r_t\to r$. Let $0<\kappa<1$ and assume $j+(r-j)/\kappa\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{conv}P)$. For all sufficiently small $t$, there is an exponential erosion of $E_t$ with radii $s_t\exp(v_t\cdot(z-j))$ removing exactly mass $\kappa\delta_t$ and exactly first base moment $\delta_t(r_t-j)$ about $j$. All fibers in $P$ remain positive, so the new source has base centroid $j$ and mass $m+(1-\kappa)\delta_t$. For fixed $\kappa$, existence is uniform with respect to desired loss means in any compact subset of $\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{conv}P)$ as the fibers and $\delta_t$ converge.
title: Exponential inner erosion restores an integer base centroid with exact small loss
